acceptance: Input SHA and original H4 cohort/label identity
Common function rows labels weights identical
Target labels cannot change scores; reversal gives aligned identical scores
Clean new-directory replay byte-identical science CSVs
aggregation: Paired source contrasts; equal-source average within India, then equal-country average over eleven primary countries. Report mean, min/max, sign counts (zero tol1e-10). Both secondary targets separately.
allocation: H4 descending score, exact-score tie blocks share uniform fractional probability to meet expected weighted quota. No identifier/outcome tie-break.

cohorts.common_functions: Intersect H4 planning cohort with valid administration MOST one-hot and complete adoption indicators with at least one adoption; selected MOST adopted in both. Preserve H1 planning event on identical firms for both function models. Re-normalise evaluation weights mean one within this common source. No administration-specific event redefinition. Compare B, B+planning MOST5, B+administration MOST5 and B+both MOST5 (secondary diagnostic).
cohorts.planning_H4: Exactly H4 planning matched MOST/adoption cohort; H1 productivity event labels fixed before matching. Logistic B/MOST re-estimated as parity check; tree B/MOST sensitivity.

composition: Sector and employment (<20,20-99,100-249,>=250,UNKNOWN) shares and within-group contact rates; total variation of shares and expected weighted individual-contact allocation between function models. Expected allocation distances are not realised list overlap/Jaccard.
contrasts: H4 planning MOST increment B+planningMOST minus B for logistic and tree, separately
On common firms, administrationMOST minus planningMOST, separately per learner
On common firms, each function and both functions increment versus identical B
Tree minus logistic increments only as sensitivity, not winner selection
features: H4 B=sector a5a, founding/start year a6, multi-establishment s4, foreign ownership a3b. No employment/sales/country/region/target event as predictors. Same H4 valid domains and UNKNOWN.
functions: Both function MOST categories represented as five nominal one-hot states; no ordinal risk constraint. MAX validity needed only for matched eligibility, not as a model feature in H5.
known_exposure: All H4 results and historical pooled/H1/H3 evidence have been inspected. H5 is a retrospective follow-up chosen after H4, with no prospective external validation or independent preregistration. No H5 matched-function fit or tree score has been computed before this lock.

models.logistic: H4 fixed L2 C=1 lbfgs max_iter2000 tol1e-8; stable per-row math.fsum prediction; no tuning.
models.one_class: Training prevalence constant; record if present.

tree.interpretation: One fixed shallow alternative learner to expose model dependence; not an optimiser or model selection exercise.

output_privacy: Only aggregate CSVs, model parameters, membership hashes, QA and code. Never raw records, firm IDs or per-row prediction vectors.
preprocessing: Fit numeric medians and StandardScaler on training only with always unscaled missing flags. Fixed H4 categorical domains. Same encoding for logistic and tree.
preserved_primary: H4 planning logistic B_MOST5 minus B at q0.50 remains primary; H5 does not select a winning learner or replace H4 hierarchy.
sources: Identical H4 twelve primary sources, eleven countries; both India sources held out together. Both secondary targets separately scored after fitting all primary sources; never in primary averages.
training_weights: H4 equal-country and equal-source within country preserving relative base_wt, globally rescaled to sum Ntrain.
uncertainty: Descriptive retrospective finite-sample; no verified PSU/strata and no manufactured survey CIs/pvalues. No causal benefit, programme eligibility, cost savings or welfare claims.
